content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Development Environment Setup and CLI in NativeScript"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Welcome to this technical tutorial on setting up your development environment for NativeScript and mastering the NativeScript Command Line Interface (CLI). Before building cross-platform native applications for iOS and Android, you must configure your local machine with the correct dependencies, runtimes, and tools."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and System Requirements"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To develop NativeScript applications, your system needs specific core tools installed. Depending on whether you target Android, iOS, or both, the requirements vary slightly."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Node.js: Download and install the latest LTS version of Node.js from the official website."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Java Development Kit (JDK): Version 17 or later is required for Android development."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Android Studio: Required for Android SDKs, build tools, and the Android Emulator."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Xcode: Required exclusively for iOS development on macOS."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing the NativeScript CLI"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The NativeScript CLI is the primary tool you will use to create, build, run, and manage your applications. Install it globally on your system using npm by running the following terminal command:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"npm install -g nativescript"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"After the installation completes, verify that the CLI is correctly installed and check your system setup by running the doctor command:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"ns doctor"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The \"ns doctor\" command scans your environment, identifies missing dependencies or misconfigured paths, and offers suggestions to resolve them."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a New NativeScript Project"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once your environment passes the doctor check, you can create a new project. NativeScript supports plain JavaScript, TypeScript, Angular, and Vue. To create a new application using TypeScript, run:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"ns create MyFirstApp --ts"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Navigate into your newly created project directory using the terminal:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"cd MyFirstApp"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Running Your Application"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"To run your application on an emulator or a connected physical device, use the run command followed by the platform target."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"ns run android"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Or for iOS (macOS required):"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"ns run ios"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also add the \"--bundle\" flag for optimized builds or use live reload for instant updates during development:"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"ns run android --bundle"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully configured your development environment, installed the NativeScript CLI, and learned how to initialize and run a cross-platform application. You are now ready to build rich native user interfaces using NativeScript."}]
